blocks.packageReason: Package, justified: the stat that gets raised is picked inside apply from the highest Attack and highest Sp. Atk among the standing foes, so there is no plain condition to pull out and no fixed stat for the stat-stage effect. 1 attr: Spyware (5597 attr 0: stages 2, Defense, Sp. Def). The three settings sit together in the private `opts` object, so each param reads it through `path: opts` with its own codec. Behaviour kept as it is: showAbility is always true, so the popup shows on entry even when no foe stands (canApply is false then, so it does not); the comparison uses the highest value of each stat ACROSS foes, which can mix two different foes; a tie goes to the physical answer. Oddity, not fixed: the stats are read with getStat(stat, false), i.e. without stat stages. The raise goes through a normal StatStageChangePhase on the holder itself.

feasibility: At least one foe must still be standing
Only damaging moves count as an attack; a status move or doing nothing counts as idle
The foe must be able to be switched out (the same checks as a forced switch)
Does nothing in a simulated preview
blocks.packageReason: Package, justified: the class keeps one idle counter and one history mark PER FOE (Symbols on the foe object), advances them on every end of turn and then forces the switch, which is memory plus effect. 1 attr: Strikeout (5614 attr 0, turns 3). The `idleTurns(foe)` helper exists only for tests. Oddities, not fixed: (a) the counters live on the foe's object and are never cleared when that foe leaves the field on its own, so a foe that switches out and back in resumes its old count although the comment says a fresh foe starts clean; (b) the two Symbols are shared by every holder of this class, so two holders in one battle would both advance the same counter each turn (the second sees no new history, counts the turn as idle and adds one more); (c) the attack test looks at move-history entries, so a foe that is asleep or flinched adds no entry and counts as idle. Simulated calls do nothing.

blocks.packageReason: Package, justified: the multiplier is a continuous formula of the holder's missing HP, so it is neither a fixed stat multiplier nor an HP threshold; the formula is the class's multiplierAt. Tier A because there is no closure or gate to bind (the parent gets no condition). 2 attrs: Last Stand (5338 attr 0 Defense, attr 1 Sp. Def, both 1.0 to 1.6). The same formula is repeated by hand in abilities/pressure-vessel.ts (its own class, outside this batch). Oddities, not fixed: (a) the HP fraction is hp / maxHp clamped to 0..1 with plain float math, so the values at 50% and 25% are exactly the dex points only for even max HP; (b) the parent's `multiplier` stays 1, so code that reads it (the studio's runtime reflection) sees 1, not the formula; (c) the multiplier is applied on every stat query, including AI previews. The L1 grid covers HP at every boundary; B09/chunk3.test.ts also checks multiplierAt over a range of HP values for the rebuilt attr.
